# Clear-TempFiles

Safely deletes old temporary files and reports how much space was freed.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Changes the system** | Yes |
| **Supports `-WhatIf` / `-Confirm`** | Yes |
| **Admin rights** | Only with `-IncludeWindowsTemp` |
| **PowerShell** | Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+ |
| **Source** | [scripts/Clear-TempFiles.ps1](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/scripts/Clear-TempFiles.ps1) &middot; [tests](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/tests/Clear-TempFiles.Tests.ps1) |

## Description

Removes files older than a given number of days from the user's temp folder (and optionally the Windows temp folder). Files that are in use are skipped, not forced. Empty sub-folders left behind are removed.

Supports -WhatIf to preview exactly what would be deleted and -Confirm to approve each deletion. Returns a summary object with the number of files found, deleted and skipped, and the space freed.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Path` | String[] | `@($env:TEMP)` | One or more folders to clean. Defaults to the current user's temp folder ($env:TEMP). |
| `-OlderThanDays` | Int32 | `7` | Only files last modified more than this many days ago are deleted. Default 7. Use 0 to include all files. |
| `-IncludeWindowsTemp` | switch |  | Also clean C:\Windows\Temp (requires an elevated session). |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Clear-TempFiles.ps1 -WhatIf
```

Shows which files would be deleted and how much space would be freed, without deleting anything.

```powershell
.\Clear-TempFiles.ps1 -OlderThanDays 14
```

Deletes user temp files not modified in the last 14 days.

```powershell
.\Clear-TempFiles.ps1 -IncludeWindowsTemp -Confirm:$false
```

From an elevated prompt, cleans both temp folders without prompting.

## Notes

Works on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+. Related KB: KB-013 Computer Is Running Slow, KB-017 Windows Update Fails to Install.
